claim: For the Kapitaniak–Mohammadi–Mekhilef hidden-attractor flow \(\dot x=z\), \(\dot y=-x-z\), \(\dot z=\tfrac{1}{10}x+5y-z+xy-\tfrac{3}{10}xz+a\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies, with \(q=\int x^2\,d\mu\), \(\int x\,d\mu=\int z\,d\mu=\int xz\,d\mu=0\), \(\int xy\,d\mu=-q\), \(\int yz\,d\mu=q\), and the exact stationary height law \(\int y\,d\mu=-a/5+q/5\). Moreover \(\operatorname{Var}_\mu(y)\ge q\), with equality if and only if \(\mu\) is the equilibrium point mass at \(E_a=(0,-a/5,0)\). Hence every non-equilibrium compact stationary state has \(\int y\,d\mu>-a/5\), \(\operatorname{Var}_\mu(y)>\int x^2\,d\mu=5(\int y\,d\mu+a/5)\), and positive mass in the half-space \(y>-a/5\); every nonconstant periodic orbit obeys the corresponding time-average identities.

correctness.rationale: The core mean law follows from the exact polynomial identity \(LG=a+5y-x^2\), verified independently by packaged rational polynomial arithmetic. The covariance identities follow from three elementary Lie derivatives. The variance inequality is the nonnegativity of \(\operatorname{Var}(x+y)\), and equality rigidity follows from invariance of the measure support and \(d(x+y)/dt=-x\). The proof uses no finite-time experiment to establish the theorem.
